'''Terence Meaden''' is an English retired physicist and an author who writes on [[archaeoastronomy]], mostly focusing on the megalithic sites of [[Avebury]] and [[Stonehenge]] in England, and the [[Drombeg stone circle]] in Cork, Ireland.  Meaden is influenced by the work of [[archaeologist]] [[Marija Gimbutas]] who wrote about the [[Goddess]] worshipping [[Neolithic]] and [[Bronze Age]] cultures of "[[Old European Culture|Old Europe]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6Qb4AEdZkGg |title=Terence Meaden Moon Goddess in the Land|website=YouTube.com |accessdate=2019-03-23}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Meaden was born in Wiltshire and attended [[Trowbridge High School|Trowbridge Boys' High School]].<ref name="dec" /> He has a doctoral degrees in physics from the [[University of Oxford]] and a master's degree in applied landscape archaeology from the same university.

==Hieros gamos==

Meaden argues it was the power of a strong religious narrative that underlies the purpose of these megaliths. [[Drombeg stone circle]] is based on the cosmological fertility drama of the marriage of the sky God and earth Goddess known to the Classical Greeks much later as the [[hieros gamos]]. He states that the same principles also explain the placement of megaliths at Avebury and Stonehenge, although both sites are now damaged and incomplete.  Fertility symbolism explains the religious elements behind the culture of the farming communities who were dependent on the timely arrival of seasonal weather and the fertility of crops, livestock and women.<ref>{{cite web|title=Journal of Lithic Studies of the University of Edinburgh. (2017) Volume 4, Number 4.|website=journals.ed.ac.uk |url=http://journals.ed.ac.uk/lithicstudies/issue/view/160/|accessdate=23 March 2019}}</ref>

In pre-literate times, [[Neolithic British Isles|Neolithic]] people expressed meaning through images and symbols displayed at stone circles. Meaden determined the core idea behind the building of Stonehenge and Avebury by spotting and interpreting key symbolism.  A documentary filmed in 1998 for Channel 4 and the Discovery Channel detailed his hieros gamos concept.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jh7Qve6QY-0 |title=Stonehenge - Secrets of the Stones - 1998 |website=YouTube.com |date=27 March 2011 |accessdate=2019-03-23}}</ref>

At Stonehenge on midsummer morning, a phallic shadow is cast from the "Heel" stone; this penetrates to the centre of the monument where its tip touches the "Goddess" stone.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BGfmGkUJQ68 |title=Stonehenge - Ancient Astronomical Shadow Effects and Fertility Symbolism |website=YouTube.com |date=7 December 2018 |accessdate=2019-03-23}}</ref> In his book, "Stonehenge, Avebury and Drombeg Stone Circle Deciphered", he wrote that most stone circles were planned as sunrise fertility monuments, and so need to be studied at sunrise.<ref name=dec>{{cite web|title=Deciphering-stone-circles-Drombeg-and-Stonehenge|website=oxford.academia.edu |url=http://oxford.academia.edu/TerenceMeaden/Deciphering-stone-circles-Drombeg-and-Stonehenge/|accessdate=23 March 2019}}</ref>

Meaden writes that the Neolithic calendar was based on the eight festival dates of traditional agriculture, corresponding roughly to the pagan [[Wheel of the Year]].<ref name=dec/>

Meaden studied Drombeg in 2018, writing: "The [[summer solstice]] marks the occasion of the consummation of the classic Marriage of the Gods, uniting the Sky Father with the Earth Mother. This act of consummation between stones representing divinities was devised as an action spectacle for the Neolithic people".<ref>{{cite web|title=Dr Terence Meaden's Research into the Core Meaning of Axial and Recumbent Stone Circles|website=silentearth.org |url=https://www.silentearth.org/dr-terence-meadens-research-into-the-core-meaning-of-axial-and-recumbent-stone-circles-by-shadow-casting-at-sunrise//|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224114141/https://www.silentearth.org/dr-terence-meadens-research-into-the-core-meaning-of-axial-and-recumbent-stone-circles-by-shadow-casting-at-sunrise/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=February 24, 2020|accessdate=31 May 2019}}</ref>
